# Decisions: commit-attribution

- 2026-08-13T08:01:32.455Z — rule: **Never record push, merge, or PR state as an event — derive it from git at read time. Only commit-to-initiative attribution is recorded.** — chose **Split the model: RECORD commit-to-initiative attribution in the log, DERIVE pushed/merged from git at read time. A commit's initiative never changes, so the recorded half can never go stale; push state changes constantly (force-push, rebase, branch deletion), so recording it would strand a false fact in an append-only log the moment anyone rewrites history.** over Recording push/merge/PR state as events alongside the attribution — the obvious symmetric design, and the one that silently rots. Also over deriving BOTH halves from git at read time, which cannot work: git has no idea which initiative a commit belongs to, and that is precisely the fact only sofar holds. because git is truth for git state; the log is truth for intent. Duplicating the first into the second is how a record starts lying. The whole point of this initiative is a staleness signal a session can trust — a signal built on recorded push state would itself be the next thing to go stale.
- 2026-08-13T08:01:40.172Z — chose **Attribute each commit individually, at commit time, when the session pin already names the initiative. Exact by construction.** over Deriving a phase's commits from session-boundary HEAD shas (record HEAD at session start; the range is startHEAD(N)..startHEAD(N+1)) and filtering that range by the initiative's file_touched set. Proposed and rejected inside the same design conversation on 2026-08-13. because The range design is a heuristic, and its two failure modes are fatal to gap 1. Concurrent sessions share this worktree, so any range contains peers' commits and the file-set filter is a guess that mis-attributes whenever two initiatives touch the same file — which the adjacency data says is the normal case here, not the edge case. And a claim like "this initiative's work is all pushed" cannot rest on a guess: a wrong "your work shipped" is worse than no signal, because it retires a next action that was never done. Separately, closing the range at session end is an off-by-one that would eat the most important commit of every session, since CLAUDE.md mandates write-back BEFORE the final commit.
- 2026-08-13T08:01:48.217Z — rule: **The review step names existing skills for code-quality checks and never reimplements them; sofar emits the prompt and records the verdict, never analyses code and never calls a model.** — chose **The review step is instruction text plus a record-derived evidence packet. sofar renders what to review, against which decisions, over which diff — and names the existing skills (/code-review, /simplify) for the code-quality half. The model reaches for those skills; sofar ships no analysis code and makes no model call.** over Building bug-hunting, edge-case and code-quality analysis into sofar itself — which would duplicate mature tools badly and drag a record-keeper into being a code analyzer, against CLAUDE.md's guard-rails. because Same pattern as the SessionStart digest: sofar injects text, the model acts. It keeps SPEC §Architectural invariants intact (zero model API calls) while still buying a real review. The one check with NO substitute is conformance to the record — whether the shipped code honoured the standing constraints and stayed out of the rejected approaches — because sofar is the only thing that holds them; /code-review cannot know a given decision exists.
- 2026-08-13T08:11:51.978Z — rule: **The commit-to-initiative binding lives in a `Sofar-Initiative:` commit trailer and is READ from git — never recorded as an event, and never inferred from timestamps or file overlap.** — chose **1.1 capture mechanism: the commit-to-initiative binding lives in a `Sofar-Initiative: <slug>` COMMIT TRAILER, written by the agent at commit time and read back from git with `git log --format='%(trailers:key=Sofar-Initiative,valueonly,separator=%x2C)'`. sofar appends NO event about commits and stores no sha. Ruled by the user 2026-08-13.** over A PostToolUse hook on `git commit` (the originally planned option, now dead on arrival); a git post-commit hook installed by sofar; git notes; and dropping exact attribution to keep only the branch-level pushed signal record-integrity 4.4 already ships. because PostToolUse capture would reintroduce the exact defect record-hygiene D1 exists to prevent: logging git makes the record un-settleable, since the commit OF the record appends an event about committing the record — confirmed empirically in repo.md M2 ("write back, commit, and the tree is dirty again with command_run"). And record-integrity D6 already rejected per-commit attribution outright, because it "needs state the record deliberately does not keep" and time-window attribution misreads interleaved parallel sessions. A trailer is neither: it is not recorded state and not a time-window guess, so it clears both objections while keeping the established principle — read git, never log it. Git notes were rejected as fragile where it matters most: they need their own push refspec, are dropped by most tooling, and a normal clone sees nothing, which defeats the cross-session sharing that is the entire point. Probed on git 2.50.1 before deciding: cherry-pick preserves the trailer, rebase preserves it, and an untrailered commit reads back as empty rather than as a guess — which hands task 1.3 its visible-never-guessed surface for free.
- 2026-08-13T08:18:55.078Z — rule: **Never attribute a commit from the branch binding. When no session resolves, leave it unattributed and visible — a wrong attribution is worse than a missing one.** — chose **2.1: a `prepare-commit-msg` git hook injects the trailer automatically. It reads CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID from the inherited environment, resolves it to the initiative with the EXISTING homeInitiative (mcp/context.ts:174, already imported by cli/event.ts), and appends `Sofar-Initiative: <slug>` if not already present. It must be idempotent for amend, and must exit 0 unconditionally — a hook that can fail a commit is worse than no attribution.** over Instructing the agent to type the trailer (the plan's original assumption); a git commit template; a `sofar commit` wrapper subcommand; and a prepare-commit-msg hook that resolves the initiative from bindings.json instead of the session. because Proven empirically this session, not assumed: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is present in the agent's shell, matches the real session id exactly, and IS INHERITED by a git hook — a probe hook wrote the live session id into a commit message. That makes attribution automatic rather than remembered, which is the only thing that closes the leak: an instruction is forgettable, and a forgotten trailer is a silent unattributed commit that quietly degrades the 3.2 staleness signal. A commit template was rejected because it is inert for `-m` and `-F`, which is exactly how agents commit. A wrapper was rejected for fighting muscle memory and owning a git surface forever. The bindings.json variant was rejected by live counter-example: main is bound to drift-certification while this session works in commit-attribution, so it would have stamped the WRONG slug on both of this initiative's commits — and homeInitiative is the resolver record-integrity D13 already fixed for this precise failure. Consistent with record-integrity D2: the home is derived from the logs, never from a duplicated index.
